primitives.name: Multi-Entity Attention Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: In this paper, we introduce baller2vec, a multi-entity generalization of the standard Transformer that, with minimal assumptions, can _simultaneously and efficiently_ integrate information across entities and time.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'X': 'set of entity states at time t', 'Q': 'query matrix of shape (B, T, d_k)', 'K': 'key matrix of shape (B, T, d_k)', 'V': 'value matrix of shape (B, T, d_v)', 'd_k': 'dimensionality of keys', 'd_v': 'dimensionality of values', 'B': 'batch size', 'T': 'number of time steps'}
primitives.assumptions: Entities lack natural ordering; attention is symmetric across all pairs of entities.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When entity cardinality exceeds model capacity or temporal resolution becomes insufficient.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's probabilistic state transition kernel via attention-weighted expectation over entity embeddings.
layer2.telemetry: Attention head activation consistency during pass prediction.

primitives.name: Trajectory Distribution Encoder
primitives.verbatim_quote: Given that entities lack a natural ordering, how do you effectively model interactions between entities across time?
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'z_t': 'discretized spatial location vector at time t', 'z_{t+1}': 'next location vector', '\\mathcal{E}': 'entity embedding set', '\\mu_{t+1}': 'mean of next location distribution', '\\Sigma_{t+1}': 'covariance matrix of next location'}
primitives.assumptions: Trajectories follow a multivariate Gaussian distribution within discrete grid cells.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Highly multimodal or non-Gaussian motion patterns lead to underfitting.

layer2.mapping: Encodes player and ball movement into GSE's state transition function using learned spatial-temporal kernels.
layer2.telemetry: KL divergence between predicted and actual trajectory bins.

primitives.name: Player Identity Embedding
primitives.verbatim_quote: Not only does baller2vec learn to perform these tasks well, it also appears to "understand" the game of basketball, encoding idiosyncratic qualities of players in its embeddings, and performing basketball-relevant functions with its attention heads.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'e_i': 'embedding vector for player i', 'f_{\\theta}': 'learnable function parameterized by θ', 'p_i^{\\text{pos}}': 'position coordinates of player i', 'p_i^{\\text{role}}': 'role identifier (e.g., guard, forward)', 'p_i^{\\text{stats}}': 'statistical features (e.g., speed, shooting accuracy)'}
primitives.assumptions: Player identity is preserved across time and can be encoded via static and dynamic features.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Loss of distinctiveness in embeddings when roles or stats are highly correlated.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's actor-state representation for decision-making and role-based behavior modeling.
layer2.telemetry: Cosine similarity between embeddings of same player across sessions.

reasoning_traces.think:
baller2vec introduces a novel transformer variant designed for multi-agent spatiotemporal modeling. It extends the standard self-attention mechanism to accommodate multiple entities without requiring fixed ordering. This allows for efficient parallel processing of interactions among players and the ball over time. The core innovation lies in treating each entity as a node in a dynamic graph, where attention weights dynamically reflect interaction strength. Mathematically, this is expressed through a generalized attention kernel that operates on entity-specific query-key-value matrices. The model avoids sequential dependencies typical of RNNs, enabling scalable training. Its ability to encode player identities and predict complex behaviors like passing demonstrates emergent understanding of game structure. Failure modes include misalignment of attention heads when entities exhibit unexpected behavior or when temporal resolution is inadequate for capturing fast-paced actions.
